assumptions: the flag byte in rdx (sort entry) and the rdi object passed by both callers are not interpreted: the flag's nonzero meaning and the rdi object's role are not in the pinned code
the sorted order is the order the virtual slot +0x30 key comparison plus the slot +0x10 tie-break define; the element type and the key's meaning are not in the binary
the heap sift-down picks the right child over the left child when the two children compare equal; the choice between equal children does not affect the sorted result
the container's heap table is already allocated with room for every element before the sort runs; no allocation happens inside the pinned code

callers.args: rdi = -0x1b60(%rbp); rsi = -0x1bb8(%rbp) (count); rdx = movzbl -0x1bb0(%rbp) (flag byte); rcx = lea -0x1ac0(%rbp) (container)
rdi = -0x1628(%rbp); rsi = -0x1608(%rbp) (count); rdx = movzbl -0x1634(%rbp) (flag byte); rcx = lea -0x1590(%rbp) (container)

comparator.global_source: RELATIVE relocation at 0x64ecfb0 with addend 0x5d48410; file bytes zero
comparator.key_slot: vtable +0x30 on the element's +0x40 object, called twice on the first element and once on the second; the compared values are the int32 results
comparator.rule: returns 1 exactly when key(first) < key(second), 0 when key(first) > key(second); on equal keys it checks the second element's vtable slot +0xd0 against *(0x64ecfb0): on a match it calls slot +0x10 on (object + 0x20) and returns the sign bit of the result, on a mismatch it calls the +0xd0 slot itself with (object, first element pointer, second element pointer, 0, 0) and returns the sign bit of that result
comparator.unknown: the function at 0x5d48410 and the identities of the virtual targets are not pinned

container.heap_pointer: base + 0x110; the stored pointer aims at the slot for element 32, so slot i > 31 sits at heap - 0x100 + i * 8
container.rule: slot i is read from the inline table when i <= 0x1f and from the heap table otherwise; every pinned routine uses this split
container.size_observed: the sort entry works on a count passed in rsi; no capacity or count field is read by the pinned code

rule: returns at once when the flag byte in dl is nonzero, and when the count in rsi is zero
builds two range structs on the stack (container at +0x00, range start 0 at +0x08, container at +0x10, count at +0x18) and calls the introsort loop with depth 2 * bsr(count)

when count <= 0x10 calls the insertion-sort pass once over the whole range; otherwise calls it over the first 0x10 elements and then calls the single-element step once per index from 0x10 to count - 1
returns void; canary at rsp+0x28 checked on the normal path, failure calls __stack_chk_fail
range [begin, end) comes from the two structs (+0x08 each); a range of 0x10 or fewer returns at once, leaving it for the insertion-sort tail
a zero depth jumps to the heapsort fallback at 0x5d4c6c4; otherwise the depth is decremented once per level
pivot selection moves the median of (first + 1, mid, last - 1) into first, using the less-than predicate in the exact arm order recorded in callers.tsv

Hoare partition around the pivot now at first, with inline element swaps; the low cursor advances while its element is less than the pivot and the high cursor retreats while the pivot is less than its element
after the partition the left half recurses through the self-call at 0x5d4c682 and the right half is processed by the tail loop back to 0x5d4c239

heapsort fallback: make_heap by sifting down from (n - 2) / 2 to 0 through 0x5d4bce0, then sort_heap by swapping the root with the last element and sifting the new root down, until one element is left
canary at rsp+0x98 checked on the small-range return and the heapsort return; failure calls __stack_chk_fail
hole index in rsi, range length in rdx, value in rcx; the value belongs to the hole at entry
sift-down: the larger child (right child 2 * hole + 2 when it exists and is not less than the left) is moved up until the hole reaches a leaf; a lone left child is moved up when the length is even
push-up: the value is walked back up toward the hole it started in, moving each smaller parent down, and is stored where the walk stops
comparisons use the same virtual key comparison and tie-break as the predicate; no canary
loads element[rcx] from the container in rdx and element[rsi] from the container in rdi, both through the inline/heap slot split
reads both keys through the virtual slot +0x30 on each element's +0x40 object; returns 1 when the first key is less, 0 when it is greater
on equal keys applies the tie-break recorded under comparator (slot +0x10 path on a vtable match, indirect +0xd0 call otherwise) and returns its sign bit
returns its result in al; pushes r13/r12/rbp/rbx, 8 bytes stack reserve, no canary
exchanges the handles at (container rdx, index rcx) and (container rdi, index rsi), each through the inline/heap slot split
pure swap: no calls, no stack frame, no canary; returns void
range [start, end) from the two structs (+0x08 each); returns at once when start equals end
for each index i from start + 1 to end - 1: compares element[i] with element[start] through the virtual key comparison and tie-break
when element[i] is less than element[start], shifts the whole prefix [start, i) right by one slot and stores element[i] at start
otherwise calls the single-element step for i, which walks element[i] down into its place
canary at rsp+0x38 checked on the normal path; failure calls __stack_chk_fail
index in *(rdi + 0x08), container in *(rdi); the element at the index is the value being placed
walks the value down: while it is less than the element one slot below (virtual key comparison plus tie-break), that element is shifted up one slot and the hole moves down
stores the value in the hole once it is no longer less than the element below it, or the hole reaches slot 0
the step has no lower-bound check: its callers only reach it when the element at the range start is not greater than the value, so the walk stops at the start at the latest
no canary; pushes r15/r14/r13/r12/rbp/rbx, 0x18 bytes stack reserve

inferences: the entry plus the introsort loop plus the insertion-sort tail is the libstdc++ std::sort shape for this container: __introsort_loop with depth 2 * log2(n), threshold 16, median-of-three pivot, Hoare partition, make_heap/sort_heap fallback, then __final_insertion_sort
the container reads as a small-buffer-optimized vector of 8-byte element handles with 32 inline slots; the element type and the key's meaning are not in the binary
the rdi object the callers pass and the sort entry never reads is plausibly the comparator object, since every comparison goes through the elements' own virtual slots instead
